152.title: Foxx Begins Hearing to Hold Northwestern, Rutgers, and UCLA Accountable for Antisemitism on Campus
152.description:
Since the barbaric attack on October 7, antisemitism—verging on support for Hamas terrorism—has seen a drastic rise on college campuses across the nation. Recently, at least 50 U.S. college campuses have been grappling with anti-Israel and antisemitic protestors occupying college campuses with encampments. Many university administrators have been left paralyzed in response or have given in to protestors' demands.

Today, Education and the Workforce Committee Chairwoman Virginia Foxx (R-NC) delivered the following statement at a hearing titled "Calling for Accountability: Stopping Antisemitic College Chaos."

187.title: The Virginia Foxx Story
187.description:
One year ago, Rep. Virginia Foxx was chosen to lead the Committee on Education and the Workforce one final time.

This is the story she shared with her colleagues, and a list of wins the Committee has secured for parents, students, and hardworking taxpayers across the nation to date.

The Committee on Education & the Workforce has passed legislation to:
- Lower the cost of college.
- Support the American workforce.
- Safeguard the rights of proud parents in the first ever Parents Bill of Rights.
- End China’s influence and infiltration of universities.
- Lower prescription drug costs.
- End Biden’s attack on hunting and archery in schools.
- Protect women’s sports.
- Bring more transparency to medical bills.
- Combat human trafficking.
- Stop radical and risky ESG investing with retirement funds.
- Block Biden’s student loan schemes and bailouts.

And this is not to mention the countless oversight and regulatory actions the Committee has taken to protect Americans from the abuses of the Biden administration. 

Be sure to follow the Committee on Education & the Workforce to stay informed. We are fighting for you!

664.title: Rep. Kline speaks in support of Student Success Act
664.description:
02.25.15

Remarks: 
Well, good morning.

I'm John Kline. I chair the House Education and the Workforce Committee. We've got some legislation coming up this week that I think is critically important.

And it's caused me to think back -- now, back a long way to when I was a kid in school and, boy, my parents were so -- so intent on me getting through school, getting my diploma, getting to college. I had a paper route. I sacked groceries. I did all of those things to be the first person in my family to get to college and graduate.

And that's what we want for children across America. We want every child to get an excellent education in every school. And what we have right now is simply not working. We have -- in many places, half of our kids are not graduating from high school. And many of those who do graduate, they're really not ready to go to college or go to work.

We need to change the status quo. And what we have up this week is legislation to do that. It's a bold step to take us in a different direction, to return control to parents and local school boards and states, and get away from this one-size-fits-all mandate program that we have coming from the federal government now.

So, I'm excited about it. I'm excited about the changing course. And I'm excited about giving every child a chance to succeed.

John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the U.S. House Education and Labor Committee, speaks on the floor of the House in opposition to H.R. 3221, a plan that would orchestrate a complete government takeover of student lending and a massive string of new entitlement spending.

968.description: Part of a special series introducing the Republican Members of the U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Education and Labor.

969.title: Kline Keeps Fighting to Fully Fund Special Education
969.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN) speaks out on the need for Congress to finally meet its decades-old promise to pay the federal government's fair share of special education costs under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA). Reps. Kline and Todd Tiahrt (R-KS) forced a vote on their proposal to add $1 billion in additional funding for FY 2010 by redirecting funding from other duplicative, unnecessary, or lower priority programs; Democrats rejected the plan.

970.title: Kline Continues Fight to Fully Fund IDEA
970.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, criticizes the decision to block debate on an amendment that would have increased funding for the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. Along with Rep. Tiahrt, Kline was seeking to increase funding for the program by $1 billion.

971.title: Small Businesses Want Health Care Reform
971.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, participates in a hearing of the Health Care Solutions Group. Asking what small businesses are looking for in health care reform, he is told: "More choice, more competition ... without taking over the whole system and making small business owners pay for it."

972.title: You Have Not Yet Suffered Long Enough
972.description: Richard Baker, a Canadian citizen and founder of North American Surgery, testifies before the House GOP Health Care Solutions Group about a 28-year-old Canadian patient denied spinal surgery with the explanation: "You have not yet suffered long enough."

973.title: Kline Speaks at GOP Health Care Solutions Group Hearing
973.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, gives opening remarks at a hearing of the Health Care Solutions Group. The panel heard heart wrenching stories of Canadian and British citizens denied care under a government-run health care system.

974.title: Kline Asks: Where are the Jobs?
974.description: Nearly six months after Democrats rushed to enact a nearly trillion dollar stimulus package, Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, joins fellow Republicans in asking: Where are the jobs?

975.title: Kline Highlights CBO Critique of Democrats' Government Takeover of Health Care
975.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the House Education and Labor Committee's top Republican, highlights a breaking news report in the Washington Post detailing new criticisms by the Director of the Congressional Budget Office of Democrats' proposed governement takeover of our health care system.

976.title: Kline Statement on Democrats' Proposed Government Takeover of American Health Care
976.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, joined other committee Republicans in voicing opposition to proposed Democratic legislation that would orchestrate a government takeover of our nation's health care system. Republicans want to make health care more affordable, reduce the number of uninsured Americans, and increase quality at a price our country can afford.

979.description: Rep. John Kline (R-MN), the top Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, joins other congressional leaders to demand a full and open review of cap-and-trade legislation that Republicans warn could kill jobs and drive up energy prices.

980.description: Rep. John Kline gives his opening statement at a HELP Subcommittee consideration of a pair of partisan bills that would impact Americans ability to save for retirement by making 401(k) plans more complex and costly while reducing workers access to individualized investment advice.

Tom Price, M.D. (R-GA), the top Republican on the U.S. House Workforce Protections Subcommittee, delivers opening remarks during a hearing on proposed leave mandates for American workplaces. 983.title: Rep. Kline Rejects Government-Controlled Single Payer Health System

1103.title: Republican Leader Boehner - The Employee Free Choice Act
1103.description: The cleverly-entitled Employee Free Choice Act would kill secret ballot voting rights in union organizing elections and make employees' votes public through what's known as a "card check."  In card check campaigns, union bosses gather authorization cards purportedly signed by workers expressing their desire for a union to represent them -- a process that notoriously leaves workers open to coercion, pressure, and outright intimidation.  Led by Rep. Howard P. "Buck" McKeon (R-CA), House Republicans vigorously fought this undemocratic bill to protect the private voting rights of working Americans.
